headline: Bank of Japan Raises Rate to Its Highest Level in 31 Years, but Doubts About the Yen Persist
summary: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to its highest level in 31 years, accelerating hikes to counter price increases from the Middle East war. Internal dissent and government opposition persist.
why: The Bank of Japan sets monetary policy for Japan, and its rate path influences the yen, Japanese bond yields and global carry trades.
why_moved: The rate increase aims to counter price rises from the Middle East war, though internal dissent and government opposition remain.
